newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks steady on select industrial demand.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks steady on select industrial demand.

text.p: Jordanian stocks held up well on Sunday despite thin trade on the back of floor trader's demand on select industrials led by Livestock and Poultry, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index shed a slight 0.05 percent to 144.27 points from 144.34 points on Saturday.
Dealers said prices were held firm by continued select demand on Livestock and Poultry, with nearly a fifth of total turnover on the firms and a handful of other industrials.
The stock has seen buying interest by an single Gulf based investor reported to have been gradually building up his stake since last week, some dealers said.
Steady demand on Arab Bank, heavily weighted in the official 60-share index, helped to further underpin trade.

The exchange's weakness sent the index below 140 points at the end of June, sliding to levels not reached since 1993, mainly blamed on high interest rates diverting investors to more attractive instruments and minimal institutional support.

A total of 383,299 shares changed hands on Sunday in a moderate 515,879 dinar turnover in the cash-squeezed market. Of 42 stocks traded, 13 advanced, 19 fell and ten were unchanged. Two posted year lows.
"Trade was not in the large quantities that traders hoped for and the focus was on Livestock and Poultry and few stock that represented 70 percent of trade," said one broker.

Investment sentiment has been improving since the government announced last week a package of economic reforms in the wake of recent unrest fueled by the government's doubling of bread prices in line with IMF-agreed economic reforms.
The Pearl Investable Index -- an independent index of the 45 best-performing shares from the official market -- firmed 0.07 percent to 81.08 points. It was 15.11 percent down on last year.

In industrials, the leading sector, Jordan Cement Factories shed 10 fils to 3.380 dinars with a few dealers saying there were no signs of the recent limited foreign buying on the stock which the government plans to sell part of its majority stake.
Livestock and Poultry rose 20 fils to 590 fils on a large 131,237 dinar turnover. Dar-al-Dawa rose 50 fils to 4.70 dinars.
In services, Jordan Electric Power was unchanged at 1.540 dinars and National Portfolio rose 10 fils to 1.210 dinars.
In banks, volume was light, with Arab Bank's 500 fils rise to 232.000 dinars still supporting the market.

Industrials dominated on Sunday, with a 322,715 dinar turnover and an index drop of 0.21 percent, banks had a 150,744 dinar turnover and an index rise of 0.07 percent while services had a low 41,424 dinar turnover and an index drop of 0.03 percent.
A total of 130,944 shares worth 74,359 dinars changed hands in thin trade in the parallel market.
